sheetDescription: Every problem with a written explanation, a video walkthrough, and an editor that checks your answer.

steps.title: Learn the Basics
steps.description: Reading input, printing output, and the shape of every problem that follows.

problems.title: Print a Number
problems.statement:
Complete `printNumber`, which reads a single integer from the input and prints it.

This one exists to get the mechanics out of the way: how you read input, how you print, and what the editor does when you press Run. Every problem after this assumes you have done it once.

**Printing, by language**

| Language | Statement |
| --- | --- |
| C++ | `cout << value;` |
| Java | `System.out.print(value);` |
| Python | `print(value)` |

**Constraints**

- `-1000 <= value <= 1000`
hints: You need to read the value before you can print it. In C++ that is `cin >> value`.
Print the value and nothing else — no label, no trailing text. The checker compares your output exactly.

check.prompt: If the input is 0, what should the output be?
check.explanation: Nothing is being transformed — whatever comes in goes straight back out, zero included.

approaches.intuition:
Read one integer, print it. There is no algorithm here, which is the point: the whole cost of the problem is knowing where input comes from and where output goes.

The function reads its own input rather than taking a parameter, so you are seeing the raw shape of a competitive-programming main loop before we start hiding it behind signatures.

testCases.explanation: The value is echoed back with nothing around it.

problems.title: Sum of Two Numbers
problems.statement:
Read two integers and print their sum.

The interesting part is not the addition. It is that the two values arrive on the same line, separated by a space, and your reader has to cope with that — which is how most input you will meet is shaped.

**Constraints**

- `-10^9 <= a, b <= 10^9`
- The sum can exceed a 32-bit integer, so pick your type accordingly.
hints: Two successive reads from the same stream will happily cross a space — you do not need to split anything by hand.
Both inputs fit in 32 bits. Their sum does not. In C++ that means `long long`, in Java `long`.

approaches.intuition: Read both values, add, print. The only trap is the type: two values near 10^9 sum to near 2×10^9, which overflows a signed 32-bit integer and silently wraps to a negative number. Widening the accumulator is the whole problem.

testCases.explanation: Signs are not special — the same two reads handle them.
